scope.description: Required with items: "first_task", "continuation" or "new_task" (see the tool description). Omit on advance / done / start updates.

session.description: When you delegated this step to a session you started: that session's short name (from start_session's result). The app shows its live state on the step.

items.description: The whole plan, in order (1–12 steps); replaces the previous list.

tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: ask or propose it, and call this.

Your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, which the recap never replaces. Never write it before this call, where it can reach the user cut to a short summary. The result says whether the box shows your question: ask in the message only a question it does not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label is the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to fix, commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status. It must stand on its own, since it is also read away from the transcript and the box draws under anything you write after this call: never point at anything else in the conversation ("listed below", "see above", "in my message").

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead (to act here on what this turn found, say), an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Like the recap, never point at anything else in the conversation. Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence. A click sends it to you as the user's answer. No leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

input.description: That tool's input — same shape you'd pass when calling it directly. For computer items whose action is left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key or type, and for form_input items, include action_summary in the item's input, as you would when calling that tool directly.

actions.description: List of tool calls to execute sequentially. Example: [{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"left_click","ref":"ref_12"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"type","text":"hello"}},{"name":"computer","input":{"action":"screenshot"}}]

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'press_key' presses a hardware key 'count' times: return, delete (backspace), an arrow, select_all, undo or redo (a key also hides the on-screen keyboard); 'set_appearance' switches the device to light or dark mode; 'appearance' says which it is in; 'set_keyboard' shows or hides the on-screen keyboard (it appears only while a text field has focus, and 'press_key' and 'text' hide it again); 'rotate' turns the device a quarter turn left or right ('direction'); take a 'screenshot' after it and tap in that screenshot's frame, however it comes back; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

points.description: For 'touch_path': touch path samples in device points. First point is touch-down; last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

points2.description: For 'touch2_path': two-finger path samples in device points. Each sample carries both contacts (x1/y1, x2/y2); first is touch-down, last is touch-up. dt_ms is the delay before that sample (0-1000 ms; the first sample's is skipped, so send 0 or omit it; at most 30 seconds in all).

duration.description: Seconds. For 'tap', >0.5 is a long-press. For 'swipe', the gesture duration (default 0.3).

key.description: For 'press_key': the key or edit command to press.

content.content:
# Readings — kernel-defs (spec v0 §21–§75, §79–§81)

Modules: `formal/Ern/MemoryModel/Access/{Basic,Ops,Invariants}.lean`.
Machine-checked witnesses quoted below: `scratchpad/kd/Readings.lean` (W1–W4) and the `Examples`
section of `Invariants.lean` (E-63.8). Full path of the scratch file:
`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-guygouri-Devlab-ernlang-ern/c986905c-e900-4fd9-bebc-4a3ce7ebb180/scratchpad/kd/Readings.lean`
(checked with `lake env lean`, no error).

Each entry: clause, quote, reading used, alternative, example whose verdict changes.
"[policy]" marks a reading fixed by `policy.md` (recorded as required); the others are mine.

## A. Spec problems (need arbitration)

**SP-A1 [blocking for §57, transfer] §63 admits an ownership cycle.** Policy removes the draft clause
`(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst`. W1 (decide): statics `src`(0, Init), `prov`(1, Init);
`alloc(prov, owner src)` → place 2 owned by 0; `alloc(prov, owner 2)` → place 3 owned by 2;
`TransferPre K0 c2 0 3` holds (all fields, §63.8 included). After the step places 2 and 3 own each
other: root 2 is active, held by unusable place 3 (§49.8 false) and covers leaf 2 of unusable place 2
(`NoDangling` false). §58 ("must ... preserve the relevant invariants") vs §63's clause list. The next
wave's `transfer_preserves` is false as stated for these definitions.

**SP-A2 §71.2 vs §36 [policy: record].** §71.2 "permitted through exercisable `Modify` or a valid
`writeShared` over `SharedMutable` metadata"; §36 "Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant
the right to create ... exclusive authority over the administered storage". `AllocStatic.providerRight`
follows §71.2 literally: `alloc` can create a root `Modify` authority with only an `Observe` right on a
`SharedMutable` provider. Example: provider leaf `SharedMutable`, an `Observe` derivative held by the
frame and no `Modify` on it: §71.2 accepts, §36 forbids.

**SP-A3 §69.2/§70.3: descendants of authorities released by the effect [policy for §69; by analogy
for §70].** W2 (decide): `x`, `r` leaves; `a := derive(root x, [x], Modify)`; `store(a, r)`;
`b := derive(a, [x], Observe)`; `endUse(r)` is accepted and leaves `b` active with inactive origin
`a`. §51 "linked to a valid origin": holds if valid = exists (our `I2`), fails if valid = active.
The `free` analogue (owned `q` instead of `r`) behaves the same.

**SP-A4 §75 StaticPinnedBottom domain.** "Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places directly
owned by the base frame". Reading: only static indices (`l < statics.length`). Alternative (draft): every

# VI. Abstract Authority Machine

The components described below constitute the logical state of the sequential discipline. They prescribe neither generalized runtime metadata nor reference syntax.

## 38. Machine State

The access discipline is based on the finite state

\[ S_3=(F,P,I,A,D) \]

where `F` represents the frame stack, `P` the places, `I` their initialization, `A` the authorities, and `D` the validity anchors. Administrative states of arenas and other library abstractions are separate from `S₃`. The external contract `K` is a separate parameter. The internal representation may carry auxiliary information that creates no new rights.

## 39. Execution Frames

`F` is a nonempty stack of identified, non-duplicate frames. Every frame except the initial frame knows its parent. Frames hold temporary authorities and directly local places. The **current frame** is at the top of the stack. `ancestor(f₁, f₂)` means `f₁` is `f₂` or an ancestor of `f₂` in the stack and its call chain.

The base frame, whose identity is 0 in states reachable from the initial state, never exits. An exited frame can neither be the terminal owner of a usable place nor hold an authority that remains active. Frames have semantic existence; no particular runtime representation is required.

## 40. Logical Places, Leaves, and Ownership

A place has an identity, optionally a structural parent, an abstract `kind`, an owner `owner : Frame | Place`, and a logical death marker. Structural parenthood `partOf(p,q)` describes the subplaces of a value; `owner` describes **who keeps the storage** of a root place valid. An owned place may lie outside its owner's direct footprint; ownership and composition are therefore distinct.

A **leaf** is a place with no structural children. `footprint(p)` contains the leaves of `p`, and access rights over a place are evaluated on those leaves. Places transitively owned by a value are not automatically leaves of its `footprint`. A logical unit of the access discipline does not automatically constitute an additional allocation in the elementary memory machine.

A place `p` is **usable** (`Usable(s,p)`) if and only if:

1. `p` exists and is not marked dead;
2. if its owner is a frame, that frame belongs to the stack;
3. if its owner is a place `q`, then `q` is itself usable and the chain terminates at a frame in the stack.

An ownership cycle makes no place usable. `placeFrame(p)` is the terminal frame of this chain when `p` is usable. Structural parts share their parent's owner and death marker. A value may be logically ended by `endUse` without the place that contained it becoming unusable; the substorages it owned may, however, die.

A **root place** has no structural parent. Every root place has a root authority of own mode `Modify`, with no origin, held exactly by that place's owner (`RootHeld`). This authority cannot be transferred in isolation; root ownership follows a legal transfer of the owning value when necessary.

## 41. Leaf Initialization States

Every tracked leaf has exactly one of the states `Uninit`, `Init`, or `Moved`.

- `Uninit`: no initialized value available in this leaf.
- `Init`: initialized value, subject to type, representation, and storage obligations.
- `Moved`: value consumed by transfer, inaccessible as its former value.

Aggregates may be partially initialized. Both `Uninit` and `Moved` prohibit ordinary reads, while remaining distinct states for diagnostics and end-of-use obligations. An initialization state creates no access permission.

## 42. Authorities, Modes, Holders, and Origins

An authority conceptually has the following fields:

```text
Authority {
    id
    mode: Observe | Modify
    origin?: AuthorityId
    footprint: Set<Leaf>
    holder: Frame | Place
    active: Bool
}
```

`origin` links a derived authority to its current origin. Authorities have fresh identities and well-formed origin chains. A root authority has no origin; a derived authority has one. Creating derived rights does not increase the scope or permitted mode of the origin.

The **holder** (`holder`) is not the **owner** (`owner`). An authority derived by `derive` or `split` is initially held by the current frame; `store` or a permitted transfer may make it held by a place. The derived `issue` operation proceeds through `split` followed by `store`. `release` does not release a root. There is no persistent `Suspended` field: suspension of rights is inferred from active descendants and applies leaf by leaf.

## 43. Effective Rights and Exercise of Authorities

For an authority `a` and a leaf `l`, `effective(s,a,l)` is derived from the active descendants of `a` whose footprint contains `l`:

1. if `a` is inactive or does not cover `l`, its effective mode is absent;
2. if no active descendant covers `l`, the effective mode is the own mode of `a`;
3. if an active descendant with own mode `Modify` covers `l`, the effective mode of `a` is absent;
4. otherwise, when the covering active descendants are `Observe`, the effective mode of `a` on `l` is `Observe`.

The effect is **local to each leaf**: after splitting a region, the origin may retain effective `Modify` over undistributed leaves.

Requested modes are ordered `Observe ≤ Modify`. `ExercisableAt(s,a,m)` means:

- `a` is active and its own mode permits `m`;
- either `a` is held by the current frame;
- or `a` is held by a place `p`, and the current frame has, over **all** leaves of `p`, an authority itself exercisable in mode `m` with sufficient effective mode.

The latter clause is recursive along the holder chain. Thus, being active or covering a leaf does not automatically make an authority exercisable. `HasRight(s,m,p)` means the current frame has exercise in mode `m` and sufficient effective mode **over every leaf in `p`'s footprint**. Every operation requires the modes it actually needs; an authority's own mode alone is insufficient.

## 44. Dependencies and Effective Anchors

`D(p)` is the set of authorities serving as **validity anchors** for place `p`. An anchor is valid as long as the authority it names is active. Dependencies of contained values are accounted for transitively. Relevant dependencies follow the value during transfer; those of its container do not automatically follow a part transferred in isolation.

For an authority `x`, its **effective anchor** is the root reached by traversing its origin chain. It does not necessarily coincide with its current holder. Lifetime constraints are calculated from the frame of that effective anchor and the frames of places that remain usable. A dependency cannot create a right or artificially extend a lifetime.

`AnchorOrder` requires, for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, that the frame of the effective anchor of `x` be the frame of `q` or one of its ancestors. `AnchorOrderHeld` imposes the same rule on every **active authority held** by `q`. These conditions apply to the resulting states of operations that move or create holder relations.

## 45. Parameters, Returns, and Reanchoring

A call parameter is an **active derived authority held by the caller** before being passed to the callee; its original provenance may go back to an earlier frame. This interpretation does not require that the authority was originally derived in the calling frame; that additional requirement belongs to Spec 3. The caller **yields** the authority to the new frame: it does not simultaneously retain a copy. If the authority remains in that frame upon return, `exitFrame` releases it; **it is not automatically returned to the caller**. To retain its own right, the caller may pass a **fresh derivative** of the authority it wishes to keep: this is ordinary reborrowing. The definition of ergonomic calling conventions is deferred to Spec 3.

A result is returned by a legal `transfer` into the result place provided by the caller as a `Modify` parameter. Surviving authorities and their dependencies are reanchored by `exitFrame` to still-valid origins. There is no standalone correspondence `M` and no implicit escape permission.

## 46. Arenas as Library Administration States

Each entry belongs to the library's abstract state, **separate from kernel state `S₃`**. It has the following fields:

```text
ArenaEntry {
    storage: PlaceId
    internal: AuthorityId
    available: Set<Leaf>
    issued: Set<(Region, AuthorityId)>
}
```

A region is **available if and only if each of its leaves belongs to `available`**; the empty region is always available. Issuance removes the leaves of the issued region from `available`. Reset restores all leaves of the administered storage to that set. The registry and its updates belong to the abstraction contract and create no kernel permissions.

The arena is **live** if `internal` is active. The **arena value** is the place holding `internal`, distinct from the possible owner of `storage`. Administered storage may be local, static, allocated, or issued by another arena, under `newArena` preconditions and applicable invariants. `available` and `issued` remain **in the library's arena entry**.

## 47. Initial State

The kernel's initial state contains only base frame 0 and the declared static storage. Every static leaf has its declared initial state, `Init` or `Uninit`. The roots of static places directly owned by frame 0 have a root `Modify` authority held by that frame; a static may also be owned by another static, in which case its root authority is held by the latter. The initial state invents no dynamic allocation, derived authority, or implicit anchor. The initial arena registry belongs to library state and is empty. The initial frame does not exit.

## 48. External Parametric Contract

`K` contains the predicates `DeclaredDisjoint`, `SharedMutable`, `Pinned`, `ExternalDone`, `Deallocable`, `FreeCompat`, and `Satisfiable`. Their obligations are specified in Section 80. `K` can neither fabricate access rights nor remove an obligation of the Charter. The predicate `Invalidates` is not part of this contract.

# VII. Invariants of Reachable States

Machine states are subject to structural, validity, and exclusivity requirements preserved by permitted transitions under their declared external contracts.

## 49. WF3 — Well-Formedness of Frames, Places, and Authorities

`WF3(s)` is a **predicate on state `s`**. It jointly requires:

1. a nonempty, duplicate-free frame stack, every frame having a valid identity and, except for the base frame, a valid parent; frame-parent relations are well-founded;
2. a place structure whose composition links are valid and **acyclic**; every structural part shares its parent's owner and death marker;
3. valid owners of type frame or place, and **well-founded** ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place;
4. footprints consisting exclusively of leaves of existing places;
5. authorities with valid identities and modes, whose existing origins form **acyclic** chains ending at a root authority;
6. `RootChain`: every origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at the root of the **same structural root place** as that leaf;
7. `RootHeld`: every usable root place has its active root `Modify` authority, with no origin, held exactly by its owner;
8. holder validity: every active authority is held by a frame present in the stack or by a usable place.

Numerical ordering of identifiers, parent precedence over child in a list, and bounds on generated identifiers may be used **to represent or prove** this well-formedness in a formalization; they are not normative restrictions on place or authority identities. Preservation of `WF3` by a transition is a **required property of transitions**, not an additional clause of the state predicate. `WF3` does not impose any particular physical object layout: that belongs to refinement into the elementary memory machine.

## 50. I1 — Structural Exclusivity

For two active authorities **unrelated by derivation** covering the same leaf, their own modes must both be `Observe`. This rule also applies to leaves identified as `SharedMutable`; their particular mutation is governed by the `writeShared` contract and creates no exception to I1.

Exclusivity of **effective** modes (`effective_exclusive`) is a consequence of I1 and the definition of `effective`, not the definition of I1. On a leaf, two incompatible authorities cannot simultaneously possess incompatible effective rights. The only permitted independent ordinary coexistence is `Observe` / `Observe`.

## 51. I2 — Conservation of Rights

A derived authority covers only a subfootprint of what its origin chain permits and does not elevate its mode. Derivation and splitting restrictions do not allow duplication of an exclusive right over a leaf. Every active authority is linked to a valid origin according to state and reanchoring rules. Partial suspension follows from `effective`.

## 52. I3 — Validity of Anchors and Dependencies

Every explicit anchor of a still-usable place is valid. An operation cannot invalidate an anchor retained by a place that remains usable. Transitive propagation of dependencies from contained values does not change this obligation. Dependencies are not permissions and are insufficient to justify an access.

## 53. I4 — Consumption and Movement

A `Moved` leaf cannot be read as if it still contained its previous value. Moving a value does not preserve two copies of an exclusive authority. Initialization state and authority-exercise state are separate checks.

## 54. Anchor Ordering and Absence of Orphan Rights

`AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` are defined in Section 44. `NoDangling` prohibits an **active** authority from covering a leaf belonging to an unusable place; the invariant does not say that a leaf is initialized. `NoOrphan` requires every active authority held by a place to be connected to a frame in the stack through a **finite, non-repeating chain** of authorities: the first link is held by a live frame, and each active link **structurally covers the entirety** of the place holding the next link. The link need not have an effective mode over that place. `NoOrphan` guarantees neither the exercisability of all stored authorities nor freedom from blocking.

## 55. ArenaInv — Invariant of the Arena Abstraction

`ArenaInv` is an invariant of the **library contract**, not an additional predicate of kernel state. For every live arena:

- `storage` designates an existing, usable place; the footprint of `internal` is exactly the footprint of `storage`;
- `internal` is active, with own mode `Modify`, held by the arena value;
- available leaves and issued regions belong to the administered storage;
- two still-active issuances have disjoint regions; no leaf of a still-issued region simultaneously belongs to `available`;
- every still-issued block authority is a derivative of `internal` complying with exclusivity and validity rules;
- anchor and ownership restrictions are respected.

Arena entries do not, by themselves, constitute an additional storage owner. Two live arenas may cover common leaves when their `internal` authorities are distinct and their effective rights are compatible; no **global** disjointness of arena footprints is imposed.

## 56. Uniqueness of Live Administration

**An authority identity may serve as `internal` for at most one live administrative abstraction**, whether an arena, `HandlePool`, `DataStack`, or another library administrative instance. Before registering a new abstraction, its creation operation must jointly check the absence of that identity from **all relevant registries of live administrations**. Uniqueness concerns the identity of the `internal` authority, not merely possible overlap of footprints: abstractions with distinct `internal` identities are not forbidden merely because their footprints overlap. Library contracts must make the information required for this guard available to the creation operation; checking only an abstraction's own registry is insufficient.

**This guard is not a condition for any safety property in Section 57.** The effective right (Section 43, case 3) already prohibits a second issuance over leaves covered by an active block derived from the same authority. Rather, the guard preserves the **abstraction contract**: without it, simultaneous administration of the same `internal` could cause `reject` instead of `fail`, or reissue a previously released block that the first administration still considers unavailable. It creates neither permissions nor allocations and introduces no general detection of authority cycles. Its physical representation and encapsulation of library registries remain outside the kernel.

## 57. Main Invariant

\[
Inv3 = I1 \land I2 \land I3 \land I4 \land AnchorOrder \land NoDangling
\]

On states reachable from `S3.init statics` under `DDSound(K)`, the kernel guarantees:

\[
WF3 \land Inv3 \land AnchorOrderHeld \land NoOrphan
\]

`ArenaInv` (Section 55) belongs to the library abstraction: it is not included in this main kernel invariant.

I5, associated with pinned storage, remains a **specialized obligation** of `K.Pinned`, not a clause automatically implied by sequential accesses alone. This property is required for reachable states under the declared assumptions. Its correspondence with allocations and bytes requires the refinement defined below.

# VIII. Definition of Transitions and Management of Authorities

   732	theorem exR_held {s : S3} {m : Mode} {E : Nat → Bool} {a p b : Nat} {y : Authority}
   733	    (hy : s.A[a]? = some y) (ha : y.active = true) (hm : m.le y.mode) (hp : y.holder = .place p)
   734	    (hb : b < s.A.length) (hc : ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P p, Allows (effective s b l) m)
   735	    (hE : E b = true) : exR s m E a = true := by
   736	  simp only [exR, hy, ha, hp, Bool.true_and, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq,
   737	    List.any_eq_true, List.mem_range]
   738	  exact ⟨hm, b, hb, hc, hE⟩
   739	
   740	/-- `ExercisableAt` is computed by `|A| + 1` steps of `exR` (decision procedure for §43). -/
   741	theorem exercisableAt_iff {s : S3} {a : Nat} {m : Mode} :
   742	    s.ExercisableAt a m ↔ kiter (exR s m) (s.A.length + 1) a = true := by
   743	  refine ⟨fun h => ?_, exercisableAt_of_kiter s m _ a⟩
   744	  induction h with
   745	  | base hy ha hm hf => exact exR_base hy ha hm hf
   746	  | held hy ha hm hp hb hc ih =>
   747	    rw [← kiter_fix (exR_rule s _)]
   748	    have hb' := kiter_bound (exR_rule s _) _ _ ih
   749	    exact exR_held hy ha hm hp hb' hc ih
   750	
   751	/-- Decidability of `ExercisableAt` (§43). -/
   752	instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (m : Mode) : Decidable (s.ExercisableAt a m) :=
   753	  decidable_of_iff _ exercisableAt_iff.symm
   754	
   755	/-- `HasRight(s, m, q)` (§43): the current frame has an authority exercisable at `m` whose
   756	effective mode permits `m` on every leaf of `q`'s footprint. -/
   757	def HasRight (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Prop :=
   758	  ∃ a ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.ExercisableAt a m ∧
   759	    ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, Allows (effective s a l) m
   760	
   761	/-- Decidability of `HasRight` (§43). -/
   762	instance (s : S3) (m : Mode) (q : Nat) : Decidable (HasRight s m q) := by
   763	  unfold HasRight; infer_instance
   764	
   765	/-! ## Dependencies and anchors (§44) -/
   766	
   767	/-- Anchors of the value at `q`, inherited from its parts (§44: dependencies of contained values
   768	are accounted for transitively). -/
   769	def depsOf (s : S3) (q : Nat) : List Nat :=
   770	  ((List.range s.P.length).filter fun r => decide (partOf s.P r q)).flatMap s.D
   771	
   772	/-- The anchors of every place containing leaf `p` are valid, that is, active (§44; §66.3,
   773	§67.3, §68.3). -/
   774	def DepsValid (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop :=
   775	  ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, partOf s.P p q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x
   776	
   777	/-- Decidability of `DepsValid` (§44). -/
   778	instance (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (DepsValid s p) :=
   779	  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (∀ _ ∈ _, _))
   780	
   781	/-- The frame of the effective anchor of `x` (the frame of its holder) exists and is `fd` or an
   782	ancestor of `fd` (§44). -/
   783	def EffAnchorOK (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Prop :=
   784	  OptP (s.A[s.effAnchor x]?) (fun z => OptP (s.hframe z.holder)
   785	    (fun g => OptP fd (fun f => ancestor s.F g f) False) False) False
   786	
   787	/-- Decidability of `EffAnchorOK` (§44). -/
   788	instance (s : S3) (x : Nat) (fd : Option Nat) : Decidable (EffAnchorOK s x fd) := by
   789	  unfold EffAnchorOK; infer_instance
   790	
   791	/-- `AnchorOrder` (§44, §54): for every anchor `x ∈ D(q)` of a usable place `q`, the frame of the
   792	effective anchor of `x` is the frame of `q` or an ancestor. -/
   793	def AnchorOrder (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)
   794	
   795	/-- `AnchorOrder` read on the places of `P` (decision procedure for §44). -/
   796	theorem anchorOrder_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrder s ↔
   797	    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q) :=
   798	  ⟨fun h q _ hq => h q hq, fun h q hq => h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq⟩
   799	
   800	/-- Decidability of `AnchorOrder` (§44). -/
   801	instance (s : S3) : Decidable (AnchorOrder s) := decidable_of_iff _ anchorOrder_iff.symm
   802	
   803	/-- `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44, §54): the rule of `AnchorOrder` for every active authority held by a
   804	usable place `q`. -/
   805	def AnchorOrderHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
   806	  ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true →
   807	    y.holder = .place q → EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)
   808	
   809	/-- `AnchorOrderHeld` read on the places of `P` and the authorities of `A` (decision procedure for
   810	§44). -/
   811	theorem anchorOrderHeld_iff {s : S3} : AnchorOrderHeld s ↔
   812	    ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ List.range s.A.length,
   813	      OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
   814	        EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)) True := by
   815	  constructor
   816	  · intro h q _ hq x _
   817	    unfold OptP; split
   818	    · rename_i y hy; exact h q hq x y hy
   819	    · trivial
   820	  · intro h q hq x y hy ya hh
   821	    have := h q (List.mem_range.2 hq.lt) hq x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy))
   822	    simp only [OptP, hy] at this; exact this ya hh
   823	
   824	/-- Decidability of `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44). -/
   825	instance (s : S3) : Decidable (AnchorOrderHeld s) := decidable_of_iff _ anchorOrderHeld_iff.symm
   826	
   827	/-! ## Outcomes (§58) -/
   828	
   829	/-- `Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail` (§58). `fail` leaves the state unchanged and
   830	carries none. -/
   831	inductive Outcome3 (σ : Type) where
   832	  | ok (s : σ)
   833	  | reject
   834	  | fail
   835	
   836	/-- A kernel transition other than `alloc` (§58): `ok` with the effect when the preconditions
   837	hold, `reject` otherwise; never `fail`. -/
   838	inductive Guarded {σ : Type} (Pre : Prop) (eff : σ) : Outcome3 σ → Prop where
   839	  | ok : Pre → Guarded Pre eff (.ok eff)
   840	  | reject : ¬ Pre → Guarded Pre eff .reject
   841	
   842	end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

1	import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Ops
     2	
     3	/-!
     4	# Access kernel: invariants, initial state, reachability
     5	
     6	`WF3` (§49), `I1`–`I4` (§50–§53), `NoDangling` and `NoOrphan` (§54), `Inv3` (§57), the declared
     7	statics and `S3.init` (§47), `StaticPinnedBottom` (§75), and reachability from `S3.init statics`
     8	under the kernel steps O1–O16 (§57). `AnchorOrder` and `AnchorOrderHeld` (§44) are in
     9	`Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Basic`, since operations read them.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	namespace Ern.MemoryModel.Access
    13	
    14	/-! ## Root places and root authorities (§40, §49) -/
    15	
    16	/-- Root place (§40): an existing place with no structural parent. -/
    17	def RootPlace (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Prop := r < P.length ∧ parentOf P r = none
    18	
    19	/-- Decidability of `RootPlace` (§40). -/
    20	instance (P : List Place) (r : Nat) : Decidable (RootPlace P r) :=
    21	  inferInstanceAs (Decidable (_ ∧ _))
    22	
    23	/-- `RootChain` (§49.6): the origin chain of an authority covering a leaf ends at a root
    24	authority (no origin) whose footprint is the footprint of a root place containing that leaf. -/
    25	def RootChain (s : S3) : Prop :=
    26	  ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority) (l : Nat), s.A[a]? = some y → l ∈ y.footprint → isLeaf s.P l →
    27	    ∃ x z r, (x = a ∨ x ∈ s.ancs a) ∧ s.A[x]? = some z ∧ z.origin = none ∧ RootPlace s.P r ∧
    28	      partOf s.P l r ∧ ∀ l', l' ∈ z.footprint ↔ l' ∈ footprint s.P r
    29	
    30	/-- `RootHeld` (§49.7, §40): every usable root place has an active root authority of own mode
    31	`Modify`, with no origin, held by the owner of the place, whose footprint is the footprint of the
    32	place. -/
    33	def RootHeld (s : S3) : Prop :=
    34	  ∀ r, RootPlace s.P r → s.Usable r → ∃ (i : Nat) (z : Authority) (pr : Place),
    35	    s.A[i]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧ z.origin = none ∧ z.mode = .modify ∧
    36	    s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner ∧ ∀ l, l ∈ z.footprint ↔ l ∈ footprint s.P r
    37	
    38	/-- Auxiliary converse of `RootHeld` (§40, §49.7), not a clause of `WF3`: an authority with no
    39	origin is held by the owner of the root place of every leaf it covers. -/
    40	def RootHeldConv (s : S3) : Prop :=
    41	  ∀ (x : Nat) (z : Authority) (l r : Nat), s.A[x]? = some z → z.origin = none → l ∈ z.footprint →
    42	    RootPlace s.P r → partOf s.P l r → ∃ pr, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ z.holder = pr.owner
    43	
    44	/-! ## `WF3` (§49) -/
    45	
    46	/-- `WF3(s)` (§49): one field per item of §49. Index order of parents and origins represents
    47	acyclicity (§49, last paragraph). -/
    48	structure WF3 (s : S3) : Prop where
    49	  /-- §49.1: the stack is nonempty and duplicate-free, every frame below `nF`. -/
    50	  frames : s.F ≠ [] ∧ s.F.Nodup ∧ ∀ f ∈ s.F, f < s.nF
    51	  /-- §49.2: parent links are valid and acyclic (the parent precedes the child); a part shares
    52	  its parent's owner and death marker. -/
    53	  places : ∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (r : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.parent = some r →
    54	    ∃ pr : Place, s.P[r]? = some pr ∧ r < q ∧ pr.owner = pl.owner ∧ s.dead r = s.dead q
    55	  /-- §49.3: owner frames are below `nF`; owner places exist; the ownership chain of every usable
    56	  place is finite and reaches a live frame. -/
    57	  owners : (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (f : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .frame f →
    58	      f < s.nF) ∧
    59	    (∀ (q : Nat) (pl : Place) (o : Nat), s.P[q]? = some pl → pl.owner = .place o →
    60	      o < s.P.length) ∧
    61	    ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∃ f, FrameOf s q f ∧ f ∈ s.F
    62	  /-- §49.4: footprints consist of leaves of existing places. -/
    63	  footprints : ∀ (a : Nat) (x : Authority), s.A[a]? = some x → ∀ l ∈ x.footprint,
    64	    l < s.P.length ∧ isLeaf s.P l
    65	  /-- §49.5: an existing origin precedes the authority, so origin chains are acyclic and end at a
    66	  root authority. -/
    67	  origins : ∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a → a < b
    68	  /-- §49.6: `RootChain`. -/
    69	  rootChain : RootChain s
    70	  /-- §49.7: `RootHeld`. -/
    71	  rootHeld : RootHeld s
    72	  /-- §49.8: every active authority is held by a frame of the stack or by a usable place. -/
    73	  holders : ∀ (a : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[a]? = some y → y.active = true →
    74	    HolderLive s y.holder
    75	
    76	/-! ## `I1`–`I4`, `NoDangling`, `Inv3` (§50–§54, §57) -/
    77	
    78	/-- `I1` (§50): two distinct active authorities unrelated by derivation covering a common leaf
    79	both have own mode `Observe`. -/
    80	def I1 (s : S3) : Prop :=
    81	  ∀ (a b : Nat) (x y : Authority) (p : Nat), a ≠ b → s.A[a]? = some x → s.A[b]? = some y →
    82	    x.active = true → y.active = true → p ∈ x.footprint → p ∈ y.footprint →
    83	    a ∉ s.ancs b → b ∉ s.ancs a → x.mode = .observe ∧ y.mode = .observe
    84	
    85	/-- `I2` (§51): the origin of a derived authority exists; the derived mode does not exceed the
    86	origin's and the derived footprint is within the origin's. -/
    87	def I2 (s : S3) : Prop :=
    88	  ∀ (b : Nat) (y : Authority) (a : Nat), s.A[b]? = some y → y.origin = some a →
    89	    ∃ x : Authority, s.A[a]? = some x ∧ y.mode.le x.mode ∧ ∀ p ∈ y.footprint, p ∈ x.footprint
    90	
    91	/-- `I3` (§52): every anchor of a usable place is valid (active). -/
    92	def I3 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ q, s.Usable q → ∀ x ∈ s.D q, s.Active x
    93	
    94	/-- `I4` (§53, first sentence): no read of a region containing a `Moved` leaf is permitted. -/
    95	def I4 (s : S3) : Prop := ∀ (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (l : Nat), l ∈ ls → s.I l = .moved →
    96	  ¬ Read3Pre s a ls
    97	
    98	/-- `I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4` (§57). -/
    99	def Inv3base (s : S3) : Prop := I1 s ∧ I2 s ∧ I3 s ∧ I4 s
   100	
   101	/-- `NoDangling` (§54): no active authority covers a leaf of an unusable place. -/
   102	def NoDangling (s : S3) : Prop :=
   103	  ∀ (j : Nat) (y : Authority), s.A[j]? = some y → y.active = true →
   104	    ∀ q, ¬ s.Usable q → ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∉ y.footprint
   105	
   106	/-- `Inv3 = I1 ∧ I2 ∧ I3 ∧ I4 ∧ AnchorOrder ∧ NoDangling` (§57). -/
   107	def Inv3 (s : S3) : Prop := Inv3base s ∧ AnchorOrder s ∧ NoDangling s
   108	
   109	/-! ## `NoOrphan` (§54) -/
   110	
   111	/-- One link of a `NoOrphan` chain (§54): `a` is active and structurally covers every leaf of the
   112	place holding `b`. -/
   113	def CoversHolder (s : S3) (a b : Nat) : Prop :=
   114	  OptP (s.A[b]?) (fun z => match z.holder with
   115	    | .place q => s.Active a ∧ ∀ l ∈ footprint s.P q, l ∈ s.afp a
   116	    | .frame _ => False) False
   117	
   118	/-- Consecutive elements of a list are related by `R` (§54, chains of `NoOrphan`). -/
   119	def Linked (R : Nat → Nat → Prop) : List Nat → Prop
   120	  | a :: b :: c => R a b ∧ Linked R (b :: c)
   121	  | _ => True
   122	
   123	/-- `NoOrphan` (§54): every active authority held by a place ends a finite, non-repeating chain of
   124	authorities whose first link is active and held by a frame of the stack, each link covering the
   125	whole place holding the next. -/
   126	def NoOrphan (s : S3) : Prop :=
   127	  ∀ (x : Nat) (y : Authority) (q : Nat), s.A[x]? = some y → y.active = true → y.holder = .place q →
   128	    ∃ (a₀ : Nat) (z : Authority) (f : Nat) (c : List Nat), s.A[a₀]? = some z ∧ z.active = true ∧
   129	      z.holder = .frame f ∧ f ∈ s.F ∧ (a₀ :: c).Nodup ∧ (a₀ :: c).getLast? = some x ∧
   130	      Linked (CoversHolder s) (a₀ :: c)
   131	
   132	/-! ## Initial state (§47) -/
   133	
   134	/-- Declared static storage (§47): each element is (parent, owning static, kind) with its
   135	initial state, `true` for `Init` and `false` for `Uninit` (read on leaves only). -/
   136	abbrev Statics := List ((Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) × Bool)
   137	
   138	/-- Well-formed statics declaration (§47; not stated by §47, a hypothesis of the theorems on the
   139	initial state): parents and owning statics are earlier statics, and a part has its parent's
   140	owning static. -/
   141	def StaticsOK (statics : Statics) : Prop := ShapeOK 0 (statics.map (·.1))
   142	
   143	/-- Decidability of `StaticsOK` (§47). -/
   144	instance (statics : Statics) : Decidable (StaticsOK statics) := by
   145	  unfold StaticsOK; infer_instance
   146	
   147	/-- `S3.init statics` (§47): base frame 0 and the declared statics, owned by frame 0 or by
   148	another static; one root `Modify` authority with no origin per root static, held by its owner;
   149	leaves `Init` or `Uninit` as declared; no anchor, no derived authority, nothing dead or
   150	pinned. -/
   151	def S3.init (statics : Statics) : S3 :=

   153	    nF := 1
   154	    P := shapeP [] (.frame 0) (statics.map (·.1))
   155	    I := fun l => if ((statics[l]?).map (·.2)).getD false then .init else .uninit
   156	    A := (rootIdx (statics.map (·.1))).map fun i =>

   159	    D := fun _ => []

   164	directly owned by the base frame 0. A condition on `(K, statics)`. -/
   165	def StaticPinnedBottom (k : K) (statics : Statics) : Prop :=
   166	  ∀ l < statics.length, k.Pinned l →
   167	    OptP ((S3.init statics).P[l]?) (fun pl => pl.owner = .frame 0) False

   171	/-- States reachable from `S3.init statics` under the kernel steps O1–O16 (§57). -/
   172	inductive Reachable (k : K) (statics : Statics) : S3 → Prop where

   195	/-- Decidability of `K0.ExternalDone` (§48). -/

   197	/-- Decidability of `K0.Deallocable` (§48). -/

   202	/-- Three static leaves owned by frame 0 (§47): place 0 `Init`, places 1 and 2 `Uninit`. -/
   203	def st : Statics := [((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false), ((none, none, 0), false)]

   206	def s0 : S3 := S3.init st

   235	/-- §63.8 decides alone: in `s3`, the transfer of place 0 to place 1 satisfies §63.1–§63.7 and is
   236	rejected by local self-blocking prevention. -/
   237	example : (s3.Usable 0 ∧ s3.Usable 1 ∧ HasRight s3 .modify 0 ∧ HasRight s3 .modify 1 ∧
   238	    SameShape s3.P 0 1 ∧ (∀ l ∈ footprint s3.P 0, s3.I l = .init) ∧

/-- `store` as a relation (§65). -/
def StoreStep (a p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (StorePre s a p) (storeEff s a p)

/-! ## Shapes (§47, §71.1, §72) -/

/-- A local shape as a shape whose elements have no owning element (§71.1, §72: locals and
allocated storage are owned by the receiving holder). -/
def LocalShape.toShape (ls : LocalShape) : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat) :=
  ls.map fun e => (e.1, none, e.2)

/-- Owner of element `i` of a shape (§47, §72, §71): its owning element if any, `hd`
otherwise. -/
def shapeOwner (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) (hd : Holder) (i : Nat) : Holder :=
  match (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) with
  | some o => .place o
  | none => hd

/-- Places `P` followed by the elements of a shape (§47, §71, §72): (parent, owning element,
kind), owned by their owning element or by `hd`. -/
def shapeP (P : List Place) (hd : Holder) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) :
    List Place :=
  P ++ (List.range ls.length).map fun i =>
    ⟨(ls[i]?).bind (·.1), shapeOwner ls hd i, ((ls[i]?).map (·.2.2)).getD 0⟩

/-- Well-formed shape at offset `n` (§72.2, §71.1; for statics, the hypothesis recorded for
§47): the parent and the owning element of an element are earlier elements, and a part has the
owning element of its parent. -/
def ShapeOK (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Prop :=
  ∀ i ∈ List.range ls.length,
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)) (fun r => n ≤ r ∧ r < n + i ∧
      (ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1) = (ls[r - n]?).bind (·.2.1)) True ∧
    OptP ((ls[i]?).bind (·.2.1)) (fun o => n ≤ o ∧ o < n + i) True

/-- Decidability of `ShapeOK` (§72.2, §71.1). -/
instance (n : Nat) (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : Decidable (ShapeOK n ls) := by
  unfold ShapeOK; infer_instance

/-- Indices of the root elements (no parent) of a shape (§40 root places; §47, §71, §72). -/
def rootIdx (ls : List (Option Nat × Option Nat × Nat)) : List Nat :=
  (List.range ls.length).filter fun i => ((ls[i]?).bind (·.1)).isNone

/-! ## O6 `enterFrame` (§72) -/

/-- Places after `enterFrame` (§72, `ok` effect): the locals appended, owned by the new frame. -/
def enterP (s : S3) (ls : LocalShape) : List Place := shapeP s.P (.frame s.nF) ls.toShape

/-- Effect of `enterFrame(params, locals)` (§72, `ok` effect): a new frame `nF` is pushed; the
parameters are now held by it; locals are appended (uninitialized, no anchor, alive, unpinned)
with one active root `Modify` authority per root local, held by the new frame. -/
def enterEff (s : S3) (ps : List Nat) (ls : LocalShape) : S3 :=
  { F := s.nF :: s.F, nF := s.nF + 1, P := enterP s ls
    I := fun l => if s.P.length ≤ l then .uninit else s.I l
    A := mapI (fun j y => if j ∈ ps then { y with holder := .frame s.nF } else y) 0 s.A ++
      (rootIdx ls.toShape).map fun i =>
        ⟨.modify, none, footprint (enterP s ls) (s.P.length + i),
          shapeOwner ls.toShape (.frame s.nF) i, true⟩
    D := fun q => if s.P.length ≤ q then [] else s.D q
def LeafOfUsable (s : S3) (l : Nat) : Prop :=
  ∃ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, s.Usable q ∧ l ∈ footprint s.P q

/-- Decidability of `LeafOfUsable` (§66.1). -/
instance (s : S3) (l : Nat) : Decidable (LeafOfUsable s l) := by
  unfold LeafOfUsable; infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `read` of the leaves `ls` through `access` (§66). The type and storage
contract of §66.3 is not represented. -/
structure Read3Pre (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §66.1: every leaf read belongs to a usable place. -/
  usable : ∀ l ∈ ls, LeafOfUsable s l
  /-- §66.1: every leaf read is `Init`. -/
  init : ∀ l ∈ ls, s.I l = .init
  /-- §66.2: `access` is exercisable in `Observe`. -/
  exercisable : s.ExercisableAt a .observe
  /-- §66.2: the effective mode of `access` permits observation of each leaf. -/
  effectivePresent : ∀ l ∈ ls, effective s a l ≠ none
  /-- §66.3: required anchors are valid. -/
  anchorsValid : ∀ l ∈ ls, DepsValid s l

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `read` (§66). -/
instance (s : S3) (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) : Decidable (Read3Pre s a ls) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((∀ l ∈ ls, LeafOfUsable s l) ∧ (∀ l ∈ ls, s.I l = .init) ∧
    s.ExercisableAt a .observe ∧ (∀ l ∈ ls, effective s a l ≠ none) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ ls, DepsValid s l))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩⟩

/-- `read` as a relation (§66): the state is unchanged. -/
def Read3Step (a : Nat) (ls : List Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (Read3Pre s a ls) s

/-- `unpin` as a relation (§75). -/
def UnpinStep (k : K) (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (UnpinPre k s p) (pinEff s p false)

/-! ## Kernel steps (§57, §58) -/

/-- One `ok` transition of a kernel operation O1–O16 (§60–§75; §57 reachability). -/
inductive KStep (k : K) : S3 → S3 → Prop where
  | derive {s s' : S3} {src : Nat} {region : List Nat} {m : Mode} :
      DeriveStep src region m s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | split {s s' : S3} {src : Nat} {rs : List (List Nat)} :
      SplitStep k src rs s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | release {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} : ReleaseStep a s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | transfer {s s' : S3} {src dst : Nat} : TransferStep k src dst s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | depend {s s' : S3} {q x : Nat} : DependStep q x s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | enter {s s' : S3} {ps : List Nat} {ls : LocalShape} :
      EnterStep ps ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | exit {s s' : S3} : ExitStep k s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | read {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} : Read3Step a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | write {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} : Write3Step a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | writeShared {s s' : S3} {a : Nat} {ls : List Nat} :
      WriteSharedStep k a ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | pin {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : PinStep p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | unpin {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : UnpinStep k p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | endUse {s s' : S3} {p : Nat} : EndUseStep k p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | free {s s' : S3} {p auth : Nat} : FreeStep k p auth s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | alloc {s s' : S3} {pr ow : Nat} {ls : LocalShape} :
      AllocStep k pr ow ls s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'
  | store {s s' : S3} {a p : Nat} : StoreStep a p s (.ok s') → KStep k s s'

end Ern.MemoryModel.Access

# XIII. Pinning, Statics, and External Commitments

Pinning forbids certain movements or ends of lifetime. It is not a general guarantee of content immutability.

## 74. O15 — Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify` over the relevant leaves, and the operation respects applicable pinning obligations.

**`ok` effect:** A dynamic pinning obligation is installed on the relevant leaves. While it is active, `transfer`, `endUse`, `free`, and `exitFrame` are rejected if they act on leaves it pins; removal of this obligation requires `unpin` under `K.ExternalDone`. Pinning does not make contents immutable. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 75. O16 — Removal of Dynamic Pinning

**Preconditions:** `place` is usable, the current frame has exercisable `Modify`, and contract `K.ExternalDone(place)` attests that all relevant external use has ended.

**`ok` effect:** The corresponding dynamic pinning obligation ends, without itself modifying values, their initialization, or their access authorities. Static obligations are not removed by this operation. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

**Associated static rule (`StaticPinnedBottom`):** Statics designated by `K.Pinned` must be places **directly** owned by the **base frame**, not merely transitively owned by a static value. This restriction ensures that they do not die when an intermediate frame exits.

# XIV. Arenas and Collective Invalidation — Reference Abstraction
# XVI. External Contracts and Interfaces with Other Specifications

Declarative contracts create no rights. Their satisfaction is an obligation of the language, typing, implementation, or a safe abstraction, according to the nature of each contract.

## 80. Parametric Contracts of the Access Discipline

A contract `K` parameterizes rules of the access discipline without fabricating permissions. A safe abstraction using part of `K` must prove or fulfill the corresponding obligation; an unestablished precondition is not a language guarantee.

| Contract | External obligation |
|---|---|
| `DeclaredDisjoint` | `DDSound(K)`: no falsely declared disjoint region when leaves can overlap |
| `Pinned` | I5, prohibition of incompatible physical moves; `StaticPinnedBottom` for pinned statics |
| `SharedMutable` | Applicable shared-mutation discipline, with correct rights and synchronization |
| `ExternalDone` | External use of storage has ended when `unpin` is permitted |
| `Deallocable` | The place belongs to a unit that can actually be freed |
| `FreeCompat` | Opaque deallocation authority is compatible with the unit being freed |
| `Satisfiable` | The provider can satisfy the requested shape **in the current state** |

Structural conditions of `free`, dependencies, and the derived library `reset` carry the relevant invalidation obligations. Physical justification of `DDSound` must be established by a realization consistent with memory layouts and Section 82.

## 81. Boundaries Remaining to Be Specified

This specification **does not by itself determine**: concurrency and synchronization effects (Spec 2); control-flow analysis, `defer`, and by-value calling conventions (Spec 3); representation criteria and typed formation of accesses (Spec 4); representation of library metadata, address width, encodings, and alignment/ABI obligations (Spec 11); or final translation of `noalias` properties (Spec 13). Leaving a rule open does not authorize a safe interface to cause UB; the implementation must fulfill or reject the obligations before exposing the operation to safe code.

# XVII. Correspondence Between Access Discipline and Memory Machine

A transition of the access discipline must admit a realization compatible with the bytes and allocations of the memory machine. An abstract definition of a right does not suffice to justify its concrete representation.
## 23. Disjointness and Splitting

Simultaneous modifications of disjoint regions are permitted when their independence and the validity of their dependencies are established. A safe abstraction may decompose a modification authority into several authorities over independent footprints, without duplicating exclusive rights or creating rights greater than those of the origin.

This capability is modeled by the kernel operation `split` (Section 61, O2). Disjointness may be structurally guaranteed, statically proved, or justified by a prior dynamic check encapsulated in a safe abstraction, including correctly justified internal unsafe operations. For `DeclaredDisjoint`, the normative condition is **leaf disjointness**; under a memory layout satisfying `LayoutWF`, it implies disjointness of the corresponding bytes. Merely asserting disjointness without justification does not authorize splitting.

The existence of the semantic `split` operation does not determine intrinsic language syntax.

  /-- §64.2: `anchor` is active. -/
  anchorActive : s.Active x
  /-- §64.3: the effective anchor's frame is the frame of `result` or an ancestor. -/
  anchorOrder : EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q)

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `depend` (§64). -/
instance (s : S3) (q x : Nat) : Decidable (DependPre s q x) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable q ∧ HasRight s .modify q ∧ s.Active x ∧ EffAnchorOK s x (s.pframe q))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩⟩

## 64. O5 — Explicit Attachment of an Anchor

**Preconditions**

1. `result` is a usable place over which the current frame has exercisable `Modify`.
2. `anchor` designates an active, valid authority representing a real dependency of the relevant rights or storage; a declared dependency cannot extend an origin's lifetime.
3. Existing anchors are preserved and the addition respects `AnchorOrder`: the effective anchor's frame is the frame of `result` or an ancestor thereof.
4. Every dependency carried by a contained value remains represented in the transitive obligations of its container.

**`ok` effect:** `anchor` is added to `D(result)`; the container's transitive dependencies account for it. No additional access right is created. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

A safe interface must declare dependencies covering those actually required by its implementation; the annotation itself is not presumed true. An unsafe abstraction bears the obligations of its contract.

## 65. O8 — Controlled Storage of an Authority

## 66. O9 — Safe Reading of Regions

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf being read belongs to a usable place and is `Init`.
2. `access` is an authority exercisable in `Observe` mode over the region; its **effective** mode actually permits observation of each leaf being read.
3. Required anchors are valid, and the type and storage contract permits this read.

**`ok` effect:** The logical read succeeds, without modifying `F`, `P`, `I`, `A`, `D`, or arena entries. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

`Moved` and `Uninit` cannot be read. This definition does not replace concrete representation and pointer checks of the elementary memory machine.

## 67. O10 — Ordinary Write

**Preconditions**

1. Targeted leaves belong to usable places, and `access` is exercisable in `Modify` mode with **effective** `Modify` right over each leaf.
2. No incompatible ordinary authority holds an incompatible effective mode over the written leaves (I1).
3. Anchors and constraints of the relevant types, storage, and abstractions remain valid.

**`ok` effect:** The logical write sets the actually written leaves to `Init` and does not modify authorities or their anchors. An unwritten leaf does not become `Init` by this effect. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

## 68. O11 — Write Under Shared Mutation

**Preconditions**

1. Every leaf in the region is usable and declared `K.SharedMutable`.
2. `access` is exercisable in a mode **at least** `Observe` and has a present effective mode on every leaf, either `Observe` or `Modify`; exercising an authority without an effective mode is insufficient.
3. Dependencies are valid and the particular shared-mutation discipline guaranteed by `K.SharedMutable` applies.

**`ok` effect:** Actually written leaves become `Init`; authorities and their structural exclusivity I1 do not change. **Other outcome:** `reject`.

`writeShared` may update metadata under an `Observe` authority when the contract permits. Stability of observed contents is not automatically guaranteed, and this kernel **does not prove** the absence of data races: that requires the concurrency model's guarantees.

## 58. Transition Outcomes

Every operation has a conceptual outcome among:

```text
Outcome3 = ok(new_state) | reject | fail
```

`reject` means that the static discipline does not permit the step; it is neither an implicit runtime trap nor `ub` in the elementary memory machine. `fail` is a **defined failure** leaving the state unchanged; **only `alloc` may produce it in the O1–O16 kernel**. Other kernel operations produce `ok` or `reject`. Library-abstraction operations, including `issue` (§77), may define their own `fail` cases. Where such failure is provided, static preconditions are checked before dynamic availability, according to the operation's contract.

An `ok` transition must satisfy its preconditions, apply exactly its prescribed effects, and preserve the relevant invariants. No transition fabricates a permission to make its conclusion true. Holder and anchor changes are evaluated in the **resulting state** when a rule explicitly so provides.

## 59. Implicit Preservation of Modes and Anchors

Changes in effective authority are **derived** from active authorities and their origins; no `Suspended` indicator is mutated. Access operations do not change an anchor without an explicitly authorized effect of transfer, `depend`, `store`, release, or reanchoring. Leaves becoming `Init` do so through a permitted write (`write3`, `writeShared`, `store`, including during a derived `issue`) or a transfer from a corresponding source leaf already `Init`; leaves initialized in `S3.init` are declared as such.

## 60. O1 — Derivation of an Authority

# Formalization design

Decisions for the Lean formalization. They govern how to formalize, never what ERN means: semantics comes only from `specs/`. Agents follow them. A design question not settled here is proposed in the report, never decided silently.

## Goal

Check that the spec's rules deliver what ERN promises. A rule that cannot be formalized or proven as written is a result: report it with the failing goal, never work around it.

Three results stay distinct: the formal model of the rules, the theorems proven about that model, and later the correctness of the compiler against it. This formalization covers the first two.

## Architecture

The formalization uses two permanent, complementary models linked
by a refinement theorem.

This is an architectural decision about formalization, not a
normative decision about ERN semantics. Both models must faithfully
represent the validated specifications.

If a specification cannot be represented faithfully, the mismatch
must be reported. Any necessary change to the formalization
architecture requires an explicit revision of this document.

1. **Abstract model.** Memory is a set of places: variables and field paths (`p.right`). Gives the semantics of safe code. States what safe code may assume about memory.
2. **Concrete model.** Memory is byte-addressed allocations. Gives the semantics of safe and unsafe code. Parameterized by a layout interface, never by a fixed layout.
3. **Refinement theorem.** Links the two models. It is the formal statement of ERN's safety promise.

## Concrete memory

- Bytes are abstract: each byte carries its initialization state and, when it belongs to a pointer, its provenance. Address and provenance are distinct.
- The concrete model represents every distinction the spec's rules rely on, including storage shared by several places.

## Layout interface

- Size, alignment and position of each component of a type are abstract functions.
- Their guarantees (in bounds, non-overlapping where the spec requires it, aligned) are hypotheses carried as structure fields or typeclass assumptions, never Lean `axiom`s.
- The interface contains only guarantees that some spec rule needs. Each hypothesis cites the rule that requires it.
- Non-vacuity: whenever the interface changes, a layout satisfying it is exhibited and proven. An unsatisfiable interface would make every refinement result empty.
- Realizability for every admissible target and instance is an obligation of the charter's ABI and layout step. It stays recorded as open until that step discharges it.

## Main theorems

- **Observable behaviors** are defined explicitly: termination with its observable result, trap, undefined behavior, divergence. Refinement compares concrete behaviors projected onto abstract observations.
- **Abstract safety.** A program accepted by the static rules has no undefined behavior in the abstract model.
- **Refinement.** For every layout satisfying the interface: if each unsafe region satisfies its contract, every observable behavior of an accepted program in the concrete model projects to a behavior of the abstract model. Concrete safety follows from abstract safety.
- **Unsafe contracts.** A contract is an entry condition and an exit condition relating the two models. From any state satisfying the entry condition, no execution of the region reaches undefined behavior, and every non-trap exit satisfies the exit condition. A trap is terminal: it runs no cleanup and is compared as an observable behavior. The relation between the models implies the entry condition of any region reachable from safe code; a stronger entry condition must be established by the unsafe code that enters the region. Intermediate states may break the relation, since in sequential execution no other code observes them. Under concurrency, shared state is observable during the region; the contract form for that case is decided before milestone 4.
- **Scope.** Every theorem states the language fragment it covers. A theorem on a fragment supports no claim about the whole language; sequential safety implies nothing about concurrent safety.

## Construction order

1. Control flow infrastructure: abstract syntax and operational semantics of control constructs. No safety theorem yet: the control flow spec's preservation rule depends on the memory and concurrency models.
2. Memory model, safe part, on the abstract model. Abstract safety for the sequential fragment.
3. Concrete model, layout interface and refinement for the sequential fragment. The memory model counts as verified for that fragment only once refinement is proven.
4. Concurrency model: extends both models and the refinement.
5. IR dialect, once its dependencies are formalized.

The semantic style of milestones 4 and 5 and their target theorems are decided here before they start.

## Representation

- **Abstract syntax** is built incrementally: only the constructs required by the rules being formalized. No concrete syntax.
- **Semantics** is a step function where the spec is deterministic, a step relation where it is not. Interpreters for tests iterate steps with fuel. Running out of fuel is not an outcome, neither termination nor trap. Each interpreter is proven to agree with the unbounded semantics on every result it returns.
- **No Mathlib** unless a milestone requires it. Adding it is a design decision recorded here.

## 31. Nature and Transmission of Derived Accesses

A derived authority is a temporary right tied to an origin. It may be used and passed within the limits of its validity, but does not freely become a persistent value by copying its representation. Its validity depends on its origin, derivation chain, holder, and, where applicable, the anchors of a dependent value.

An authority may be held by the current frame or, in accordance with the kernel's `store` operation and derived operations such as `issue`, by a place. Such controlled placement grants no arbitrary copying, escape, or extension of validity. A value containing a derived authority may be transferred only when its anchors and rights remain valid.

## 32. Reborrowing and Restoration of Rights

While a `Modify` derivative is active, its origin cannot exercise incompatible mutation or observation through another path over the relevant leaves. During derived observations, it retains only its compatible effective rights. Its exercise capabilities are restored when the derivatives blocking them become inactive, subject to its other active descendants and the rights received from its own origin.

The active period may be determined by control flow and local use analysis; it is not automatically fixed to the entire lexical duration of a block. Control-flow analysis itself belongs to Spec 3.

## 33. Footprints and Validity Dependencies

Ordinary read and modification conflicts are evaluated over leaf footprints according to effective modes. Validity dependencies also include resources whose move, replacement, end of use, or release would invalidate an authority, even without immediate physical overlap. Operations ending or releasing a value account for transitively owned storage according to the authority machine.

A global modification of a dynamic container is presumed capable of invalidating accesses to its elements unless its contract explicitly establishes otherwise. Disjoint projections may perform independent modifications under the splitting preconditions.

## 34. Safe Splitting of Authorities

A safe abstraction may split a `Modify` authority into authorities over pairwise disjoint leaf regions. Splitting preserves invariants, prohibits duplicating competing exclusive rights, and maintains restrictions on the origin while derivatives are active.

It may be established structurally, statically, or through a prior dynamic check whose obligations remain the abstraction's responsibility. `split` is defined in Section 61 (O2); this semantic name is not a syntax decision.

## 35. Transfer and Pinning

Value transfer is prohibited when it would invalidate an active derived access. A legal transfer does not turn a second-class authority into a freely copyable persistent reference and must preserve its validity chain and anchor dependencies.

Transferring a value never physically moves storage owned by it. Moving an **in-place** leaf is rejected when that leaf is pinned; pinning only the owned storage does not prohibit transfer of the owning value. Detailed constraints belong to `transfer` (O4), `Pinned`, and pinning invariant I5.

## 36. Shared Mutation and Internal Administration

An abstraction may keep its metadata in `SharedMutable` storage and modify it through `writeShared` to the extent permitted by the applicable rights and contracts. **Shared mutation of metadata does not, however, grant the right to create, recycle, or terminate exclusive authority over the administered storage.** Such operations require `internal` to be exercisable in `Modify` mode from the value administering the storage.

For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.

## 37. Dependent Values and Persistent References

When a value depends on the validity of other storage, that dependency must be carried by an explicit mechanism. In particular, this model retains:

- joint ownership or legal transfer of the resource;
- **non-escaping** dependent values, governed by `depend`, `store`, `AnchorOrder`, and end-of-use operations; they may survive a call if their anchors come from still-valid caller resources;
- library handles checked for identity and generation upon resolution, which are not authorities by themselves;
- validity durations bound to a frame or context, without a universal system of first-class lifetimes;
- safe abstractions encapsulating, when necessary, unsafe operations and proofs of their obligations.

**Not adopted as a universal ERN mechanism:** a first-class persistent reference subject to general lifetime constraints at the type-system level. The above mechanisms are complementary; neither a handle nor a temporary access guarantees the perpetual validity of its target resource on its own.
